`husserl-thing-and-space-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/ding/001` · *constitution*
  Beginning from lower and common experience is justified because the phenomenology of straightforward perceptual experience is the foundation without which the higher constitutive problems cannot be posed.
  `husserl-thing-and-space-commentary#h3-s1-the-world-of-natural-experience-and-the-world-of-scientific-theory` · Thing and Space S 1 · [§1.   > without fear that this starting point is irrelevant to the highest problems of the constitution of scientific reality. - **introduced** · `konstitution/ding/002` · *constitution of the object in the phenomenon*
  The fundamental difficulty is named as the constitution of the object in the phenomenon: how evident assertions are possible about an objectivity not actually given in the phenomenon.
  `husserl-thing-and-space-commentary#h3-s7-preliminary-indication-of-the-method-of-the-further-investigation` · Thing and Space S 7 · [§7.   > The fundamental difficulty of the **constitution of the object in the phenomenon** comes to the fore: how are evident assertions possible about an objectivity that is not actually given in the phenomenon?

- **introduced** · `konstitution/ding/003` · *constitution*
  The task is the constitution of the identical corporeal thing in the manifold of its appearances, and all spatiality is constituted in movement of the Object and of the Ego.
  `husserl-thing-and-space-commentary#h3-s44-preliminary-indication-of-the-further-themes-of-the-investigation` · Thing and Space S 44 · [§44. Preliminary indication of the further themes of the investigation](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-thing-and-space-commentary.html#preliminary-indication-of-the-further-themes-of-the-investigation)
  > the constitution of the identical corporeal thing in the manifold of its appearances. These appearances are **appearances of movement**: all spatiality is constituted — comes to givenness — in movement, both the movement of the Object and the movement of the Ego

- **introduced** · `konstitution/ding/004` · *constitutive questions*
  The guiding questions for the rest of the lectures are put as questions of what constitutes three-dimensional spatiality, the corporeal thing in its identity, and its movement and position relative to the Ego-centre.
  `husserl-thing-and-space-commentary#h3-s44-preliminary-indication-of-the-further-themes-of-the-investigation` · Thing and Space S 44 · [§44.   > What constitutes three-dimensional spatiality in the manifold of appearances? What constitutes the corporeal thing in its identity? What constitutes its manifoldly possible movement and its position in relation to the Ego-center?

- **introduced** · `konstitution/ding/005` · *doubly constituted*
  Spatiality is doubly constituted, once visually and once tactually, so the question divides into visual space, tactile space, and the identity of the space materialized in both.
  `husserl-thing-and-space-commentary#h3-s44-preliminary-indication-of-the-further-themes-of-the-investigation` · Thing and Space S 44 · [§44.   > Since spatiality is **doubly constituted** — once with visual and once with tactile determinations (as §22 established) — the questions can be separated: how is visual space constituted, and how is tactile space constituted, insofar as they are constituted independently of one another?

  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-6-sensing-and-apperceptive-objectivation-in-acts-of-perceiving-and-pleasing` · Hua XLIII/2, S 6 · [§ 6\. Sensing and Apperceptive Objectivation in Acts of Perceiving and Pleasing](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#sensing-and-apperceptive-objectivation-in-acts-of-perceiving-and-pleasing)
  > presenting constitutes objects with respect to non-axiological predicates as *source*. Valuing constitutes, on the basis of presenting, the *axiological predicates*.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua43-2/004` · *constitutes itself*
  As spatio-temporal being constitutes itself through primary sensations, so through the feelings founded in the sensations something constitutes itself, namely values.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-1-affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding` · Hua XLIII/2, S 1 · [§ 1\. Affection, Apprehension, Turning-Toward, and Creative Act of the Understanding](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding)
  > analogously to the way in which, through (primary) sensations, *spatio-temporal* being constitutes itself, together with the apprehension-modes connected with such being — that through the feelings *interwoven with*, *founded in* the sensations, *something* constitutes itself, *namely values*.

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua43-2/005` · *constitutive*
  The schema does not embrace thinking, which is constitutive as creative consciousness for whole classes of objectivities.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-1-affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding` · Hua XLIII/2, S 1 · [§ 1\. Affection, Apprehension, Turning-Toward, and Creative Act of the Understanding](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding)
  > It does not embrace *thinking*, which is constitutive *as "creative" consciousness* for whole *classes of objectivities*

- **criticized** · `konstitution/hua43-2/006` · *constituting*
  The picture of feelings constituting values just as sensations constitute being is too narrow: it covers only the receptive level on the value-side.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-1-affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding` · Hua XLIII/2, S 1 · [§ 1\. Affection, Apprehension, Turning-Toward, and Creative Act of the Understanding](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding)
  > The picture of "feelings constituting values just as sensations constitute being" is too narrow: it covers only the *receptive* level on the value-side, leaving aside the whole spontaneous side

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua43-2/007` · *constitutive*
  The field of sensations, associations and blind motivation is constitutive for nature, and the blind motivations of the feeling- and drive-passivities are constitutive for objectivities of higher level.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-1-affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding` · Hua XLIII/2, S 1 · [§ 1\. Affection, Apprehension, Turning-Toward, and Creative Act of the Understanding](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding)
  > the *field of sensations* (which already hints at a function), of associations, of *blind motivation*, which is "*constitutive*" for *nature*, physical and psychophysical; **b)** the *field of original feeling- and drive-passivities*; and **c)** the *blind motivations belonging to them*, which are constitutive for *objectivities of higher level*

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua43-2/008` · *constitutes itself passively*
  With respect to sensation it must be said that it constitutes itself passively: time-consciousness is not executed.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-1-affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding` · Hua XLIII/2, S 1 · [§ 1\. Affection, Apprehension, Turning-Toward, and Creative Act of the Understanding](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#affection-apprehension-turning-toward-and-creative-act-of-the-understanding)
  > with respect to *sensation*, we must continue to say that it constitutes itself *passively*: time-consciousness is not "executed."

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua43-2/009` · *constitutes the unity in the immanent time-flux*
  The deepest-lying intentionality lies in the inner consciousness that constitutes the unity in the immanent time-flux, in which the enduring lived experience constitutes itself.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-4-feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality` · Hua XLIII/2, S 4 · [§ 4\. Feeling-Sensibility and Intentionality](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality)
  > *The deepest-lying intentionality* lies in the *inner consciousness* that *constitutes the unity in the immanent time-flux*. In it constitutes itself *the unitary, enduring, arising and passing-away lived experience*

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua43-2/010` · *Urbewusstsein*
  Ur-consciousness in its constitutive function is not yet an act, but the condition under which any act-content can be one enduring content at all.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-4-feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality` · Hua XLIII/2, S 4 · [§ 4\. Feeling-Sensibility and Intentionality](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality)
  > This is the layer of *Urbewusstsein* in its constitutive function — *not yet* an "act" in the act-theoretic sense, but the *condition* under which any act-content can be *one* enduring content at all.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua43-2/011` · *constitutes itself*
  Feeling and primary content form the unity of an immanent lived experience which constitutes itself in inner consciousness through the steady unity of the constituents on both sides.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-4-feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality` · Hua XLIII/2, S 4 · [§ 4\. Feeling-Sensibility and Intentionality](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality)
  > together they form the unity of an immanent lived experience*, which constitutes itself in inner consciousness *in such a way* that the *inner constituents* of the primary content and of the feeling *cover* (*decken sich*) in inner time-consciousness — namely, that the experience-unity constitutes itself through the *steady unity of the constituents on both sides*

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua43-2/012` · *constituted unity*
  The unity in inner consciousness has intentionality; the sensible sensation as constituted unity does not.
  `husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary#h3-s-4-feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality` · Hua XLIII/2, S 4 · [§ 4\. Feeling-Sensibility and Intentionality](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-43-2-studien-zur-struktur-des-bewusstseins-commentary.html#feeling-sensibility-and-intentionality)
  > has *unity in inner consciousness*, and this latter has *intentionality*; *the sensible sensation as constituted unity does not

### 1912 to 1924-1928 - Hua 4 - Ideas II

`husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary`

#### 1912 draft, written immediately after Ideas I

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/hua4/002` · *constitution*
  The 1912 manuscript treated the constitution of sense-intuitive nature and, in direct continuation, the constitution of body and soul.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-later-changes-to-this-plan` · Hua IV, editor's introduction · [Later Changes to This Plan](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#later-changes-to-this-plan)
  > The very compact presentation of the 1912 manuscript treated the constitution of sense-intuitive nature and, in direct continuation, the constitution of body and soul.

#### Husserl's annotations and appendices, 1924-1928

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/001` · *constitution of objectualities*
  Over the fifteen years of reworking, the question of the constitution of objectualities in consciousness became a central problem of Husserlian philosophy and the actual task of phenomenology became the clarification of the constitution of every reality.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-later-changes-to-this-plan` · Hua IV, editor's introduction · [Later Changes to This Plan](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#later-changes-to-this-plan)
  > The question of the constitution of objectualities in consciousness became during these fifteen years a central problem of Husserlian philosophy and gained a singular significance for phenomenology. It was no longer a matter of drafting “phenomenological sketches”; rather, the actual task of phenomenology now became the clarification of the constitution of every reality.

#### Stratum not assigned by the commentary

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/003` · *constituted*
  The objectuality is already constituted in consciousness before the theoretical acts, through certain intentional experiences and not through all experiences related to it.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s4-theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences` · Hua IV S 4 · [§4. Theoretical Acts and “Pre-giving” Intentional Experiences](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences)
  > the relevant objectuality is already constituted in consciousness before these theoretical acts, through certain intentional experiences — and not through all experiences that can be designated as related to this objectuality.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/004` · *pre-theoretical constitution*
  Feeling-experiences are themselves constitutive, constituting new object-strata, and only a turn of the theoretical glance moves them from pre-theoretical to theoretical constitution.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s4-theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences` · Hua IV S 4 · [§4. Theoretical Acts and “Pre-giving” Intentional Experiences](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences)
  > as intentional experiences they are also constitutive — they constitute new object-strata for the relevant object.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/005` · *constitutive performance*
  Theoretical acts themselves exercise a constitutive performance: categorical objectualities constitute themselves, and become theoretical objects only when the subject turns toward them.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s4-theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences` · Hua IV S 4 · [§4. Theoretical Acts and “Pre-giving” Intentional Experiences](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#theoretical-acts-and-pre-giving-intentional-experiences)
  > also exercise a constitutive performance: “categorical” objectualities constitute themselves (in a quite determinate sense: thought-objectualities), which in turn become theoretical objects only when the theoretical subject directs itself

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/006` · *constitutive synthesis*
  Already in the constitution of a sensory-spatial entity there is a hidden and analytically demonstrable constitutive synthesis, since the appearance points back to kinaesthetic circumstances.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s10-things-spatial-phantoms-and-sensation-data` · Hua IV S 10 · [§10. Things, Spatial Phantoms, and Sensation Data](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#things-spatial-phantoms-and-sensation-data)
  > we have a formation of a hidden and analytically demonstrable constitutive synthesis; for it is an “appearance” that points back to kinaesthetic “circumstances”

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/007` · *pre-givenness*
  With the pure sensation datum we encounter a pre-givenness that lies even before the constitution of the object as an object.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s10-things-spatial-phantoms-and-sensation-data` · Hua IV S 10 · [§10. Things, Spatial Phantoms, and Sensation Data](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#things-spatial-phantoms-and-sensation-data)
  > Here, with the pure sensation datum, we encounter a pre-givenness that lies even before the constitution of the object as an object.

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/hua4/008` · *constituting consciousness*
  Nature as the sphere of mere things separates itself from all other objectual spheres through a demarcation prescribed a priori in the essence of constituting consciousness.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s11-nature-as-sphere-of-mere-things` · Hua IV S 11 · [§11. Nature as Sphere of Mere Things](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#nature-as-sphere-of-mere-things)
  > through a demarcation a priori prescribed in the essence of constituting consciousness, separates itself from all other objectual spheres to be treated theoretically.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/009` · *constitutive*
  For natural objectualities a valuing consciousness has contributed nothing as constitutive to their sense-content.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s11-nature-as-sphere-of-mere-things` · Hua IV S 11 · [§11. Nature as Sphere of Mere Things](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#nature-as-sphere-of-mere-things)
  > for these objects a valuing consciousness has contributed nothing as “constitutive,” that is, to their sense-content.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/010` · *constitution of real properties*
  The constitution of real properties can also take place in higher levels, so that level-formations are possible in which higher unities attest within unities of attestation.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s16-constitution-of-thing-properties-in-manifolds-of-dependency-relations` · Hua IV S 16 · [§16. Constitution of Thing-Properties in Manifolds of Dependency-Relations](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#constitution-of-thing-properties-in-manifolds-of-dependency-relations)
  > the constitution of real properties can also take place in higher levels, so that level-formations are possible whereby in unities of attestation there in turn attest higher unities, possibly determined from them with the help of thinking grounded in experience.

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua4/011` · *constitution of material nature*
  The analyses confine themselves to the solid body, which constitutes itself as a thing with a rigid spatial shape, and this is said to be the basic piece of the constitution of material nature.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h3-s16-constitution-of-thing-properties-in-manifolds-of-dependency-relations` · Hua IV S 16 · [§16. Constitution of Thing-Properties in Manifolds of Dependency-Relations](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#constitution-of-thing-properties-in-manifolds-of-dependency-relations)
  > the solid body, which constitutes itself as a thing with a rigid spatial shape that transports itself in movement. This restriction is not arbitrary; it can be shown that we have here the basic piece of the constitution of material nature.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/012` · *constitutive functions*
  In all constitution of spatial thinghood two kinds of sensations with different constitutive functions are necessarily involved if presentations of spatial things are to be possible.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h4-a-dependencies-of-the-intuitive-characteristics-of-the-material-thing-on-the-exp` · Hua IV, ch. 3 a) · [a) Dependencies of the Intuitive Characteristics of the Material Thing on the Experiencing Subject-Body](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#a-dependencies-of-the-intuitive-characteristics-of-the-material-thing-on-the-experiencing-subject-body)
  > In all constitution of spatial thinghood, two kinds of sensations with quite different constitutive functions are involved and necessarily involved if presentations of spatial things are to be possible.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua4/013` · *constituting apprehension*
  In all constitution and at all levels there are necessarily mutually related circumstances and what belongs to them, the if-then or because-so.
  `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h4-a-dependencies-of-the-intuitive-characteristics-of-the-material-thing-on-the-exp` · Hua IV, ch. 3 a) · [a) Dependencies of the Intuitive Characteristics of the Material Thing on the Experiencing Subject-Body](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary.html#a-dependencies-of-the-intuitive-characteristics-of-the-material-thing-on-the-experiencing-subject-body)
  > In all constitution and at all levels we necessarily have mutually related “circumstances” and what “belongs” to all circumstances: everywhere we find the “if-then” or “because-so.”

#### Recorded absences

- **absent** · `husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary#h4-b-movability-and-changeability-as-constituents-of-the-material-thing-the-thing-s`
  Expected because: The section's own title calls movability and changeability constituents of the material thing, and the section immediately before it states that in all constitution and at all levels there are mutually related circumstances. No term of the family occurs in it.

  Expected because: The step from material to animal nature is the step S 11 has just prepared by demarcating nature in the essence of constituting consciousness, and the one the editor's introduction names as the constitution of body and soul. ### 1912 - Hua 5 - Ideas III

`husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary`

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua5/001` · *constitutive unities*
  Animals and human beings are seen as ensouled by things being apprehended as bodies, that is by having courses of consciousness and the constitutive unities belonging to them interpreted into them.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s1-the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy` · Hua V, Supplement I S 1 · [§1. The Constitution of the Soul (Empathy)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy)
  > which happens by certain things being apprehended as bodies — i.e. by having courses of consciousness and the constitutive unities belonging to them interpreted into them.

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/hua5/002` · *intersubjective constitution*
  The body must be apprehended as a real unity, not yet as an objective material thing through intersubjective constitution, which itself presupposes a reference to a plurality of human beings.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s1-the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy` · Hua V, Supplement I S 1 · [§1. The Constitution of the Soul (Empathy)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy)
  > The body must be apprehended as a real unity (though not yet as an “objective” material thing through intersubjective constitution, which itself presupposes a reference to a plurality of human beings

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua5/003` · *constitutes itself*
  The appearance-manifolds constituting a real thing for two subjects are different, and through interpretation they are coordinated so that the objective thing constitutes itself as the same.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s1-the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy` · Hua V, Supplement I S 1 · [§1. The Constitution of the Soul (Empathy)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy)
  > the appearance-manifold constituting a real thing for one subject and the appearance-manifold constituting “the same” thing for the other are different; through interpretation, these two manifolds are coordinated

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua5/004` · *constitutive manifestation*
  As the material body is objectified through its appearances to different subjects, so the soul constitutes itself in corresponding manifolds, through a process of constitutive manifestation and not schematization.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s1-the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy` · Hua V, Supplement I S 1 · [§1. The Constitution of the Soul (Empathy)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#the-constitution-of-the-soul-empathy)
  > Just as the material body is objectified through the manifold of its appearances to different subjects, so the soul (Sk) constitutes itself in corresponding manifolds.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/hua5/005` · *constitution of the lower experiential levels*
  Kant's problems presuppose a phenomenology and an insight into the constitution of the lower experiential levels, a task he neither grasped nor suspected in its magnitude.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s6-significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology` · Hua V, Supplement I S 6 · [§6. Significance of the Problem of Constitution; Phenomenology and Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology)
  > they presuppose a phenomenology and an insight into the constitution of the lower experiential levels — a task Kant neither grasped nor, where he brushed against it, suspected in its magnitude.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua5/006` · *problem of constitution in general*
  The problem of constitution in general, in its levels, with systematic descriptions at all levels and the exhibiting of essential connections, is foreign to Kant.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s6-significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology` · Hua V, Supplement I S 6 · [§6. Significance of the Problem of Constitution; Phenomenology and Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology)
  > The problem of constitution in general, in its levels, the necessity of carrying out the associated systematic descriptions at all levels, of exhibiting the essential connections, of considering the various a priori possibilities — all this is foreign to Kant

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua5/007` · *constituting flux*
  The ontological mode of consideration takes unities as fixed; the phenomenological-constitutive consideration takes the unity in flux, as unity of a constituting flux.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h4-s6-significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology` · Hua V, Supplement I S 6 · [§6. Significance of the Problem of Constitution; Phenomenology and Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary.html#significance-of-the-problem-of-constitution-phenomenology-and-ontology)

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua3b/002` · *constituted*

### 1917 to 1918 - Husserl, Hua 33 — Die Bernauer Manuskripte über das Zeitbewußtsein

`husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary`

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua33/001` · *constitutive relation*
  After the transcendental-phenomenological reduction the relation between absolute consciousness and sensation-datum was re-determined as a constitutive relation, sensation constituting itself in absolute consciousness as an immanent time-object.
  `husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary#h2-iii` · Hua XXXIII, editor's introduction III · [III](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary.html#iii)
  > the relation between "absolute" consciousness and sensation-datum was re-determined as a constitutive relation. Just as a transcendent object constitutes itself in the apprehension of a sensation-datum, so sensation itself constitutes itself in "absolute" consciousness as a (present, past, or future) immanent time-object.

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua33/002` · *constitutive achievement*
  The C-manuscripts deny all original constitutive achievement to the primal stream running without ego-participation: constitution of temporal objects requires an ego-achievement.
  `husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary#h2-iii` · Hua XXXIII, editor's introduction III · [III](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary.html#iii)
  > The C-manuscripts ultimately lead Husserl to deny all original constitutive achievement to the primal stream running without any ego-participation. Constitution of temporal objects is possible only when an ego-achievement is present.

- **revised** · `konstitution/hua33/003` · *constitutive significance*
  The hyletic primal stream gains constitutive significance only through a subsequent egoic act of reflection that modifies its nature.
  `husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary#h2-iii` · Hua XXXIII, editor's introduction III · [III](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-33-die-bernauer-manuskripte-uber-das-zeitbewusstsein-commentary.html#iii)
  > Only through the subsequent performance of an egoic act of reflection on the pre-intentional primal process, i.e., through an intervening modification of its nature, does the hyletic primal stream gain constitutive significance.

  > The world of nature "precedes" the immanent sphere in the constitutive order: we first have the world, and only then, through special reflective effort, can we constitute the immanent sphere as a field of objects.

### 1923-1924 - Husserl, Hua 7 — Erste Philosophie I

`husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary`

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/001` · *constituting processes*
  In the natural cognizing attitude one lives in the constituting processes and sees only their results; the processes themselves remain unseen.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea` · Hua VII, Sixth Lecture · [Sixth Lecture: The demand for a theory of cognition implied in the Platonic idea of dialectic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea-of-dialectic)
  > in the natural cognizing attitude one *lives in* the constituting processes and sees only their *results* — the identical thing, the identical proposition, the identical correctness. The processes themselves remain unseen.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/002` · *constitutive thesis*
  Every identity the cognizer has - object, proposition, truth - is a had of a having, something that makes itself in subjective life.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea` · Hua VII, Sixth Lecture · [Sixth Lecture: The demand for a theory of cognition implied in the Platonic idea of dialectic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea-of-dialectic)
  > every identity the cognizer "has" — object, proposition, truth — is a *had* of a having, an *experienced* of an experiencing, something that *makes itself* in subjective life.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/003` · *constituted unity and constituting life*
  The correlation of constituted unity and constituting life is called the core of transcendental phenomenology, and the guard is entered that makes-itself does not mean the mind invents the object.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea` · Hua VII, Sixth Lecture · [Sixth Lecture: The demand for a theory of cognition implied in the Platonic idea of dialectic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#sixth-lecture-the-demand-for-a-theory-of-cognition-implied-in-the-platonic-idea-of-dialectic)
  > This is the correlation of constituted unity and constituting life, the core of transcendental phenomenology, here derived by reflection on scientific work. The guard against the fabrication-reading: "makes itself" does not mean the mind invents the object, but that the object is constituted as the identical pole of a having.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/004` · *constitutes itself*
  It is no simple matter to understand how externality constitutes itself in the experiencing consciousness-stream and its synthetic connections.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-seventeenth-lecture-on-the-question-of-the-constitution-of-externality-the-carte` · Hua VII, Seventeenth Lecture · [Seventeenth Lecture: On the question of the constitution of "externality": the Cartesian evidence of the self-givenness of things in perception](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#seventeenth-lecture-on-the-question-of-the-constitution-of-externality-the-cartesian-evidence-of-the-self-givenness-of-things-in-perception)
  > it is nothing less than a simple matter to understand how externality constitutes itself in the experiencing consciousness-stream itself and its synthetic connections

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/005` · *sense-giving consciousness*
  Objects of every conceivable sense have their sense, constituting them as so-determined objects, out of the sense-giving consciousness.

  > have their sense — constituting them *as*, and as so-determined, objects — out of the *sense-giving consciousness*, through which they m

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/006` · *so-constituted objectivity*
  For every basic kind of objectivity the correlative basic kinds of consciousness and consciousness-syntheses must be studied as the construction in which a so-constituted objectivity constitutes itself as unity of validity.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-seventeenth-lecture-on-the-question-of-the-constitution-of-externality-the-carte` · Hua VII, Seventeenth Lecture · [Seventeenth Lecture: On the question of the constitution of "externality": the Cartesian evidence of the self-givenness of things in perception](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#seventeenth-lecture-on-the-question-of-the-constitution-of-externality-the-cartesian-evidence-of-the-self-givenness-of-things-in-perception)
  > the correlative basic kinds of consciousness and consciousness-syntheses must be studied according to their construction, in which, as consciousness-accomplishment, precisely a so-constituted objectivity constitutes itself as unity of validity.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/007` · *constitutive problems*
  Hume's theories are skeptically worthless in result, yet the problems they raise are the first transcendental formulations of phenomenology's constitutive problems.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume-but-its-ending-in-complete` · Hua VII, Twenty-fifth Lecture · [Twenty-fifth Lecture: The constitution-problem in Hume — but its ending in complete skepticism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume--but-its-ending-in-complete-skepticism)
  > Hume's theories are skeptically worthless in result, yet the *problems* they raise — above all the synthetic unity of thing and of self — are the first transcendental formulations of phenomenology's constitutive problems.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/008` · *analysis of constitution*
  The identical thing given across the changing data forces itself on Hume as the problem of synthetic unity, which phenomenology will solve through the analysis of constitution.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume-but-its-ending-in-complete` · Hua VII, Twenty-fifth Lecture · [Twenty-fifth Lecture: The constitution-problem in Hume — but its ending in complete skepticism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume--but-its-ending-in-complete-skepticism)
  > the very phenomenon sensualism cannot accommodate — the identical thing given across the changing data — is what forces itself on Hume as a problem, the problem of synthetic unity that phenomenology will solve through the analysis of constitution.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/hua7/009` · *constitutive question*
  Thing-identity and self-identity both pose the constitutive question of how an identical, in-itself-existing unity is given across a manifold of separated experiences.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume-but-its-ending-in-complete` · Hua VII, Twenty-fifth Lecture · [Twenty-fifth Lecture: The constitution-problem in Hume — but its ending in complete skepticism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-fifth-lecture-the-constitution-problem-in-hume--but-its-ending-in-complete-skepticism)
  > thing-identity and self-identity are the two great unities that sensualism dissolves and yet cannot do without, and both pose the constitutive question of how an identical, in-itself-existing unity is given across a manifold of separated experiences.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/hua7/010` · *science of constitution*
  Descartes discovered the ground but did not grasp it as the field of a descriptive, eidetic science of constitution.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-o` · Hua VII, Twenty-seventh Lecture · [Twenty-seventh Lecture: On metaphysics and theory of cognition. The significance of Leibniz's monadology and Kant's critique of reason](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-of-leibnizs-monadology-and-kants-critique-of-reason)
  > he discovered the ground but did not grasp it as the field of a descriptive, eidetic science of constitution.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/hua7/011` · *intentional analysis of constitution*
  Kant's transcendental deductions are regressive construction rather than the progressive, intuitively ascending intentional analysis of constitution that phenomenology requires.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-o` · Hua VII, Twenty-seventh Lecture · [Twenty-seventh Lecture: On metaphysics and theory of cognition. The significance of Leibniz's monadology and Kant's critique of reason](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-of-leibnizs-monadology-and-kants-critique-of-reason)
  > his transcendental deductions are *regressive construction* (arguing back from the fact of valid cognition to its presupposed conditions), with intuition only following after, rather than the *progressive*, intuitively ascending intentional analysis of constitution that phenomenology requires.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/hua7/012` · *constituting consciousness*
  The innermost sides of the constituting consciousness are scarcely touched in Kant: the sensuous phenomena he works with are already constituted unities never systematically analysed.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-o` · Hua VII, Twenty-seventh Lecture · [Twenty-seventh Lecture: On metaphysics and theory of cognition. The significance of Leibniz's monadology and Kant's critique of reason](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-of-leibnizs-monadology-and-kants-critique-of-reason)
  > The so-to-speak *innermost sides of the constituting consciousness*, Husserl says, are in Kant überhaupt scarcely touched; the sensuous phenomena with which he occupies himself are already *constituted unities*, of an over-rich intentional structure that is never subjected to a systematic analysis.

Its 1,819 words carry no term of the family.
  [§ 9. The clarification of the name "phenomenology"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-20-prolegomena-zur-geschichte-des-zeitbegriffs-commentary.html#the-clarification-of-the-name-phenomenology)

*Partial pass: SS 5, 11, 12, 13, 19 and 26. This commentary is the one place in the extracted corpus where both senses of the word stand side by side and can be told apart from the text itself: Husserlian Konstitution in SS 11 and 13, where consciousness is absolute in the order of constitution and Ideen II is read for the constitution of the spiritual world, and Seinsverfassung in SS 19 and 26, where being-in-the-world is the basic constitution of Dasein. The units below are marked accordingly in their term field. SS 1-4, 6-10, 12, 14-18, 20-25 and 27-36 have not been extracted; a pass for the theme sorge over Chapter Four already exists.*

  [Jean Hyppolite: Die Verneinung](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/lacan/lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary.html#jean-hyppolite-die-verneinung)

*Partial pass: The sessions of 13 January, 17 March and 5 May 1954 and the Gelinier presentation of the Klein paper - the places where the term family carries weight. The pass records a finding about the whole file: nothing here is Husserlian Konstitution. The register is psychoanalytic and largely ordinary - a group constitutes itself, prejudices constitute a community, Klein's 'constitutional capacity' is the hereditary sense - with the technical uses being the constitution of the Idealich, of good and bad objects, and of ignorance as a polar term. No unit carries a stratum: the commentary has no chronology.json entry, although it dates each session in its own headings.*

Lessons I-III, V-X, XII-XV, XVII-XVIII and XX have not been extracted; II and VII carry no term of the family and one is recorded as an absence. No stratum: the commentary has no chronology.json entry, although it dates each lesson in its own text.*

## Reception layer

*Read alongside the spine, not on it. A commentator's date orders the reception, not the doctrine.*

- **introduced** · `konstitution/derrida-geom/003` · *constituted*

### 1981 - Franck, Chair et corps

`franck-chair-et-corps-commentary`

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/001` · *constitution*
  Constitution as Leistung brings to light the synthetic unity of the acts of consciousness and concerns all possible types of objects, first of all the possibility of objects in general.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-four-constitutive-analysis` · [Chapter Four: Constitutive Analysis](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-four-constitutive-analysis)
  > brings to light the synthetic unity of the various acts of consciousness, delivers the object over to a pure regard, and concerns all possible types of objects, including, first of all, the possibility of objects in general.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/002` · *self-constitution*
  Constitution extends as far as the self-constitution of the ego, and constitutive syntheses define the field of all transcendental phenomenology.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-four-constitutive-analysis` · [Chapter Four: Constitutive Analysis](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-four-constitutive-analysis)
  > Constitution thus extends as far as the self-constitution of the ego, and constitutive syntheses define the field of all transcendental phenomenology.

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/franck/003` · *constitution of the object*
  The constitution of the object as formal ontology is the basis for the hierarchy of a priori levels and so for the material and regional ontologies.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-four-constitutive-analysis` · [Chapter Four: Constitutive Analysis](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-four-constitutive-analysis)
  > The constitution of the object — formal ontology — is the basis for the hierarchy of *a priori* levels and thus for material and regional ontologies

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/004` · *constitution of the ego*
  The constitution of temporality leads back to the constitution of the ego itself, without which the task of constitution would suffer from lacunae.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity` · [Chapter Five: Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity)
  > The constitution of temporality leads back to the constitution of the ego itself. Without it, the task of constitution would suffer from lacunae.

- **revised** · `konstitution/franck/005` · *absolute ipseity*
  If to constitute is always to unify, the unifying principle cannot itself be constituted: it is presupposed by all constitution and given as absolute ipseity.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity` · [Chapter Five: Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity)
  > If to constitute is always to unify, then the unifying principle cannot itself be constituted. It must therefore appear as something presupposed by all constitution and as something given in every lived experience as absolutely identical: namely, *absolute ipseity*.

- **revised** · `konstitution/franck/006` · *constitution in general*
  Withdrawing the ego from the constitution of objects does not withdraw it from constitution in general; the transcendentally absolute itself constitutes itself in a peculiar sense.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity` · [Chapter Five: Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity)
  > To withdraw the ego from one type of constitution — the constitution of objects — is not to withdraw it from constitution in general.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/007` · *constitutive system*
  The constitutive system of all objects in general is based on the constitution of the authority for which there are objects, namely transcendental subjectivity.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-six-phenomenological-idealism` · [Chapter Six: Phenomenological Idealism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-six-phenomenological-idealism)
  > the constitutive system of all objects in general is based on the constitution of the authority for which there are objects — namely, transcendental subjectivity.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/franck/008` · *pre-constituted*
  The objection is that the ego is always found in a pre-constituted world whose ontological type is known by all, and which supplies the guiding thread for describing transcendental subjectivity.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-six-phenomenological-idealism` · [Chapter Six: Phenomenological Idealism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-six-phenomenological-idealism)
  > one might object that the ego is always found in a *pre-constituted* world — a world whose ontological type, as Husserl curiously says, is "known by all" (*allbekannten*). This world supplies a guiding thread for the description of the structures of transcendental subjectivity.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/009` · *constitutional effects*
  The new epoche disregards all constitutional effects of intentionality relating to other subjectivity, delimiting the intentionality in which the ego constitutes within himself a peculiar ownness.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness` · [Chapter Eight: Flesh and the Sphere of Ownness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness)
  > we disregard all constitutional effects of intentionality relating immediately or mediately to other subjectivity, and we delimit first of all the total nexus of that actual and potential intentionality in which the ego constitutes within himself a peculiar ownness (*Eigenheit*)

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/010` · *constitution of flesh*
  The constitution of flesh is presupposed by all constitution of things, that is by all constitution of worldly transcendence in general.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness` · [Chapter Eight: Flesh and the Sphere of Ownness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness)
  > the constitution of flesh is presupposed by all constitution of things — that is, by all constitution of worldly transcendence in general.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/franck/011` · *horizons of constitution*
  The objection is put that there is no constitution of a horizon but only horizons of constitution, which marks the finitude of the phenomenological.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness` · [Chapter Eight: Flesh and the Sphere of Ownness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-eight-flesh-and-the-sphere-of-ownness)
  > there is no constitution of *a* horizon but only horizons of constitution? Does one not here run up against, in various forms, the limits that mark the *finitude* of the phenomen

- **introduced** · `konstitution/franck/012` · *constitution of the other*
  The constitution of the other is the centrepiece of the constitution of the objective world, so the analysis must determine the origin of the world's permanence.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-twelve-pairing-and-resemblance` · [Chapter Twelve: Pairing and Resemblance](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-twelve-pairing-and-resemblance)
  > The constitution of the other, Franck explains, is the centerpiece of the constitution of the objective world, which is given as a world always there and constantly present.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/franck/013` · *egological constitution*
  Since flesh is the zero-object and death belongs to its sense, the egological constitution of the world is affected by contingency.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-twelve-pairing-and-resemblance` · [Chapter Twelve: Pairing and Resemblance](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-twelve-pairing-and-resemblance)
  > the egological constitution of the world is thereby affected by *contingency*, since flesh is the "zero-object" (*Nullobjekt*)

### 1986 - Jean-Luc Marion, Sur le prisme métaphysique de Descartes — Commentary

`marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary`

- **introduced** · `konstitution/prisme/001` · *onto-theo-logical constitution*
  Seen through the prism of onto-theo-logical constitution, even the ostensibly non-metaphysical texts of the corpus release the constituted and constitutive elements of a metaphysics.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-closure-of-a-question` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, pp. 6-8 · [The Closure of a Question](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-closure-of-a-question)
  > seen through the prism of onto-theo-logical constitution, even the ostensibly non-metaphysical texts of the corpus release, like primitive colours, the constituted and constitutive elements of a metaphysics.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/prisme/002` · *Cartesian constitution of metaphysics*
  If the onto-theo-logical constitution strictly delimits the Cartesian constitution of metaphysics, it fixes that constitution's limits and in closing it opens the possibility of its overcoming.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-closure-of-a-question` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, introduction · [The Closure of a Question](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-closure-of-a-question)
  > if the onto-theo-logical constitution strictly delimits the Cartesian constitution of metaphysics, then it fixes that constitution's limits; and in closing it, it opens the possibility of its overcoming.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/prisme/003` · *constitutes himself*
  The onto-theo-logical model is used to test how Descartes constitutes himself according to a figure of onto-theo-logy, and reciprocally to subject the model to a test.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-closure-of-a-question` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, introduction · [The Closure of a Question](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-closure-of-a-question)
  > the point is not to impose it on Descartes but to use it to test how Descartes constitutes himself according to a figure of onto-theo-logy

- **revised** · `konstitution/prisme/004` · *figure of the constitution*
  Not one figure of the onto-theo-logical constitution has been found in Descartes but two, one according to cogitatio and one according to causa.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-10-a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes S 10 · [§ 10. A Redoubled Onto-theo-logy](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy)
  > not one figure of the constitution has been found but two, one according to *cogitatio* and one according to *causa*.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/prisme/005` · *concept of onto-theo-logical constitution*
  The proliferation of figures is said possibly to cast doubt on the operative rigour of the concept of onto-theo-logical constitution itself.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-10-a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes S 10 · [§ 10. A Redoubled Onto-theo-logy](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy)
  > should the proliferation not simply cast doubt on the operative rigour of the concept of onto-theo-logical constitution itself, and even on the imprudently univocal notion of *the* metaphysic

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/prisme/006` · *onto-theo-logical constitution*
  The onto-theo-logical constitution is posited to impose itself on Heidegger's thought from the two figures of metaphysics that put it most massively into evidence, Leibniz and Hegel.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-10-a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes S 10 · [§ 10. A Redoubled Onto-theo-logy](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#a-redoubled-onto-theo-logy)
  > Marion posits that the onto-theo-logical constitution imposes itself on Heidegger's thought from the two figures of metaphysics that put it most massively into evidence and into operation, Leibniz and Hegel.

- **revised** · `konstitution/prisme/007` · *onto-theo-logical constitution*
  Descartes complicates the onto-theo-logical constitution in redoubling it, and that complexification forces a decision between two hypotheses about the essence of the constitution.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-question-of-an-opening` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, pp. 373-374 · [The Question of an Opening](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-question-of-an-opening)
  > Descartes complicates the onto-theo-logical constitution in redoubling it. That complexification imposes deciding between two hypotheses about the essence of the constitution.

- **revised** · `konstitution/prisme/008` · *essence of the onto-theo-logical constitution*
  On the second hypothesis, the Cartesian redoubling reveals and deepens the essence of the onto-theo-logical constitution, of which Heidegger formulated only an elementary outline.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-question-of-an-opening` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, p. 374 · [The Question of an Opening](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-question-of-an-opening)
  > the Cartesian initiative of redoubling it reveals and deepens the essence of the onto-theo-logical constitution of metaphysics, of which Heidegger would have formulated only an elementary outline

- **revised** · `konstitution/prisme/009` · *onto-theo-logical constitution*
  Never has the onto-theo-logical constitution been so visible as in its Cartesian redoubling, precisely because it splits in two there.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-question-of-an-opening` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, p. 374 · [The Question of an Opening](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-question-of-an-opening)
  > never has the onto-theo-logical constitution been so visible as in its Cartesian redoubling, precisely because it splits in two there

- **revised** · `konstitution/prisme/010` · *onto-theo-logical constitution*
  Authenticated as a metaphysician by the onto-theo-logical constitution whose essence he discovers better in complicating it, Descartes nonetheless escapes it in part.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h2-the-question-of-an-opening` · Sur le prisme metaphysique de Descartes, pp. 375-376 · [The Question of an Opening](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-question-of-an-opening)

#### Recorded absences

- **absent** · `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-24-the-ego-undone-and-the-decentring-of-the-self`
  Expected because: The undoing of the ego and the decentring of the self is where a constituting subject would have to be met if the commentary read the Cartesian ego as one.   Expected because: The system of contradictions is the longest section of the commentary and works out the tensions of the two figures that S 10 calls two figures of the onto-theo-logical constitution. It carries no term of the family.
  [§ 19. The System of Contradictions](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-system-of-contradictions)

*Partial pass: The introduction, S 10, and the conclusion. The pass records a finding that governs the whole file: in this commentary 'constitution' is almost always the onto-theo-logical constitution of metaphysics - a Heideggerian Verfassung, the make-up or set-up of metaphysics - and not Husserlian Konstitution. Nothing in the text marks the difference. SS 1-9 and 11-25 have not been extracted; three of the longest of them carry no term of the family at all and two are recorded as absences.*

### 1994 - Rudolf Bernet, La vie du sujet: Recherches sur l'interprétation de Husserl dans la phénoménologie — Commentary

`bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary`

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/001` · *constituting consciousness*
  The reduction makes constituting consciousness appear outside the world and equally makes the world appear as constituted, the being of the world from its origin in the transcendental subject.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, p. 11 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > The reduction makes constituting consciousness appear outside the world, but it equally makes the world appear as constituted — the being of the world from its origin in the transcendental subject.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/002` · *world-constitution*
  In the leap of the reduction the transcendental subject splits into constituting subject and spectator subject, the latter observing constitution without taking part.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, p. 12 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > the subject splits into constituting subject and spectator subject. Leaping out of world-constitution, the subject installs itself in the position of the onlooker who observes constitution without taking part (*unbeteiligter Zuschauer*)

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/003` · *constituting consciousness*
  What the spectator makes appear for the first time is the ontological difference between constituting consciousness and constituted world, which the subject-world correlation covers over from within the labour of constitution.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, p. 13 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > What appears for the first time thanks to the spectator is the ontological difference between constituting consciousness and constituted world — the difference natural life misrecognizes and which the subject-world correlation covers over from within the labour of constitution.

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/bernet/004` · *constituting consciousness*
  The spectator does not produce the constituting consciousness it brings to light: transcendental consciousness constitutes the world long before and independently of any reduction.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, pp. 14-15 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > the spectator, self-produced, does not produce the constituting consciousness it brings to light: transcendental consciousness constitutes the world long before and independently of any reduction.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/005` · *constitutive activity*
  Before the reduction constituting consciousness is too buried in the world for its own constitutive activity to reveal itself to it, and lives in ignorance of itself.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, pp. 14-15 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > Before the reduction it is too deeply buried in the world and too riveted to worldly things for its own constitutive activity to reveal itself to it; in natural life it lives in ignorance of itself

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/006` · *Selbstbezug*
  The self-relation of constituting consciousness is marked by heterogeneity: it needs the spectator in order to appear to itself, while the spectator depends on nothing but itself.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, pp. 15-16 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > Constituting consciousness needs the spectator in order to appear to itself; the spectator depends on nothing but itself to reflect on its own activity as spectator.

- **introduced** · `konstitution/bernet/007` · *constituting phenomenon*
  The noema as phenomenologically reduced object is amphibolous: it names on one side a pure constituting phenomenon and on the other an object constituted unitarily in the regulated chaining of such phenomena.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object` · La vie du sujet, p. 70 · [The Noema as Phenomenologically Reduced "Object"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object)
  > The noema as phenomenologically reduced object can therefore designate on one side a pure constituting phenomenon and on the other an object-in-quotation-marks constituted unitarily in the regulated chaining of such phenomena.

- **presupposed** · `konstitution/bernet/008` · *constituted*
  The thing as constituted is essentially dependent on constituting consciousness both in its mode of givenness and in its mode of being.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object` · La vie du sujet, pp. 75-77 · [The Noema as Phenomenologically Reduced "Object"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object)
  > the thing as constituted is essentially dependent on constituting consciousness both in its mode of givenness and in its mode of being.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/bernet/009` · *qua constituta*
  If the being of the object is identified with its being-given and that with constituting consciousness, nothing seems to justify calling the constituted thing a real spatial being transcendent to consciousness.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object` · La vie du sujet, p. 77 · [The Noema as Phenomenologically Reduced "Object"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object)
  > if, as is constant in Husserl, the being of the object is identified with its being-given and the latter with constituting consciousness, then nothing apparently justifies speaking any longer of the being of the constituted thing as a real (*real*), spatial being transcendent to consciousness.

- **criticized** · `konstitution/bernet/010` · *transcendental constitution*
  Cartesian dualism obstructs any understanding of what transcendental constitution of the world by the subject means; the constituted world is neither purely interior nor purely exterior to the constituting subject.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-i` · La vie du sujet, pp. 97-98 · [I](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#i)
  > a dualism that at bottom obstructs any understanding of what transcendental constitution of the world by the subject means. The constituted world is neither purely interior nor purely exterior to the constituting subject

- **criticized** · `konstitution/bernet/011` · *acts of constitution*
  The pregiven world is not the pregiven hyle: the hyle is a formless datum preceding all acts of constitution, while the pregiven world is the sedimentation of earlier acts of formation and constitution.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-iii` · La vie du sujet, pp. 115-116 · [III](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#iii)
  > the latter is a formless sensible datum preceding all acts of constitution, whereas the former is the sedimentation of earlier acts of formation and constitution.

  `husserl-erfahrung-und-urteil-commentary#h3-s11-the-origin-clarification-of-judgment-and-genealogy-of-logic-in-the-overall-h` · Erfahrung und Urteil S 11 · [§11. The Origin-Clarification of Judgment and Genealogy of Logic in the Overall Horizon of the Transcendental, Phenomenological-Constitutive Problematic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-erfahrung-und-urteil-commentary.html#the-origin-clarification-of-judgment-and-genealogy-of-logic-in-the-overall-horizon-of-the-transcendental-phenomenological-constitutive-problematic)
  > the regress to the transcendental subjectivity constituting this pregiven world proceeds in two stages: (1) the regress from the pregiven world with all its sense-precipitates, with its science and scientific determination, to the original life-world; (2) the inquiry back from the life-world to the subjective achievements from which it itself arises.
